A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same deCIFer work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A.1–A.13 support reliable comparison despite extensive rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original deCIFer experiments on NOMA, CHILI-100K, and four CSP benchmarks, including conditioning ablations, perturbation tests, and repeated-generation analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and reports three-seed benchmark summaries. The use of simulated diffraction profiles does not negate their status as original experimental results.

M1.justification: The PXRD encoder, autoregressive transformer, conditional likelihood objective, sequence packing, attention isolation, positional resets, and optional descriptor conditioning remain unchanged. The method description is rewritten without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use NOMA, CHILI-100K, Perov-5, Carbon-24, MP-20, and MPTS-52 with the same task coverage. v4 explicitly clarifies that CHILI-100K supplies experimental structures but simulated PXRD inputs; this documents existing coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain CDVAE, DiffCSP, CrystaLLM-small, CrystaLLM-large, and U-deCIFer. The U-deCIFer rows incorporated into v4 Figure 5 reproduce comparisons already reported in v3 Figure 3 and Table 2.

E3.justification: The single-sample evaluation, perturbation settings, clean-reference transformation, model configuration, and StructureMatcher tolerances are retained. Changing the main text from training 'epochs' to 'steps' aligns it with v3 Appendix A.9 and Table 4, which already specify the same step-based schedule.

E4.justification: The conditioning ablation, noise/broadening tests, symmetry-stratified analyses, validity breakdowns, embedding PCA, and 16,000-sample Sr2Cd2Se4 case study all appear in both versions. Moving the sampling study from Discussion to Results adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports means and one standard deviation over three independent training seeds for deCIFer and U-deCIFer. External baseline values and existing Rwp distribution reporting remain unchanged. This adds training-run uncertainty reporting without establishing how many runs underlay v3.

E6.justification: Both deCIFer rows in Table 1 receive updated summaries. For example, deCIFer's Perov-5 match rate changes from 85.29 to 85.59 ± 0.38, and MP-20 from 43.51 to 44.65 ± 1.40. These replace point estimates with three-seed summaries; the principal benchmark trends and other main/appendix results remain stable.

T1.justification: The likelihood objective, masking definition, PXRD simulation equations, and matching mathematics are retained. Substituting unit weights directly into the Rwp expression is algebraically equivalent. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the experimental framing toward a controlled synthetic-PXRD baseline with basic noise and broadening, replacing broader language about realistic experimental settings. The central PXRD-to-CIF contribution and approximately 94% match-rate claim remain.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly distinguishes structural generalization on CHILI-100K from robustness to measured PXRD and identifies unmodeled effects such as background drift, preferred orientation, and multiphase mixtures. It also distinguishes training-seed variability from sampling ambiguity. Existing discussions of homometry, leakage, and conflicting compositional priors are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly states that model checkpoints are available alongside source code. Conversely, v4 omits v3's explicit AdamW beta values and attribution of benchmark train-test splits to DiffCSP. Most implementation, preprocessing, hardware, and hyperparameter details remain available.

R1.justification: v4 removes background works by Cheetham and Goodwin, Tatlier, Bunn, Oviedo, and Wang while retaining the principal generative-CSP literature. The Guo and QLoRA reference changes concern publication metadata rather than newly introduced works.

P1.justification: Most main-text sections are substantially rewritten, with expanded explanations of crystallographic workflows, synthetic evaluation, and prediction ambiguity. Experiments become an enumerated account, and the sampling-consistency discussion moves into Results. These are extensive narrative changes despite stable methods and coverage.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different page format, typography, title/author arrangement, and widespread figure/table placement. Appendix tables are redistributed, Table 1 is reformatted for uncertainty entries, and v3 Table 2 is consolidated into Figure 5. The underlying figures largely reuse existing evidence.

improvement.justification: Three-seed reporting in Table 1 and clearer limits on synthetic-PXRD validation improve the assessment of reliability and applicability. Added checkpoint-access information supports reuse, although omitted optimizer betas and split attribution reduce some reproducibility detail. With methods, coverage, and most evidence retained, the net improvement is limited.
